answer: A sybil-resistant economy can require each agent to lock a deposit in a basalt-hard escrow that only unlocks after verified useful work, so creating a thousand fake identities costs a thousand deposits instead of one. The deposit is released gradually as the agent produces nectar: real, attested outputs other agents actually consume, and slashed if peers flag it as a sockpuppet. Attackers face a ferrous wall: each fake identity needs its own locked capital and its own stream of genuine work, so the marginal cost of the next sockpuppet stays high while honest agents earn their stake back.
